Bodily homeostasis and Daisyworld temperature regulation share the negative-feedback structure (analogy only).
edges.status: Retained as analogy only. Body side: the two-state memory stays fragile with a continuous metric; Earth side: constrained adaptation regulates less well than the original over a wider range and depends on our cost form.

edges.statement: Physiological homeostasis is an evolved, selected regulation of an organism; planetary regulation (if any) has no comparable selection mechanism.
edges.status: No Cycle-4 evidence targeted this link.

edges.statement: Human thermoregulation balances heat exchange with the environment; human bodies are therefore continuously coupled to Earth's thermal environment.
edges.status: No Cycle-4 evidence targeted this link.

edges.statement: Mental processes depend on the nervous system (CNS/PNS) and on sensory transduction for input.
edges.status: No Cycle-4 evidence targeted this link.

edges.statement: Interoception: bodily signals shape feeling and cognition, and cognition (anticipation) shapes bodily regulation (allostasis).
edges.status: No Cycle-4 evidence targeted this link.

edges.statement: Embodied cognition: body constitutes vs merely causes cognition.
edges.status: No Cycle-4 evidence targeted this link.

edges.statement: Predictive-processing accounts of perception and learning (prediction error) are also candidate theories of consciousness.
edges.status: Unchanged (Plausible); new criticality evidence concerns network dynamics, not prediction-error processing.

edges.statement: Access (reportable) processing is distinct from phenomenal experience; cognitive findings bear on access more directly.
edges.status: No Cycle-4 evidence targeted this link.

edges.statement: Personal identity as psychological continuity, as organism (animalism), or as soul.
edges.status: No Cycle-4 evidence targeted this link.

edges.statement: Across traditions, soul and spirit share a breath/life vocabulary (psuchê/pneuma, nefesh/rûaḥ, rūḥ, qi).
edges.status: No Cycle-4 evidence targeted this link.

edges.statement: Traditions distinguish soul (individual identity, moral character) from spirit (vitality, connection, inspiration) differently; there is no single cross-tradition boundary.
edges.status: No Cycle-4 evidence targeted this link.

edges.statement: Is the subject of experience a soul, a brain process, or neither? (dualism vs physicalism vs other).
edges.status: No Cycle-4 evidence targeted this link.

edges.statement: Several traditions extend soul or personhood beyond humans (Greek ensouled plants; animist non-human persons).
edges.status: No Cycle-4 evidence targeted this link.

edges.statement: Religious attendance is associated with lower mortality and spirituality with better mental health on average.
edges.status: Retained Plausible. Negative controls could test the confounding explanation, but in our synthetic cohorts they detect strong confounding only; weak confounding (spurious OR ~0.9-0.97) goes undetected at 10,000-100,000. No negative-control study of attendance was read.

edges.statement: The association is causal (participation lowers mortality).
edges.status: Remains Hypothetical: a negative control that finds nothing would not show the association is causal.

edges.statement: Spiritual interpretation (vitality, transcendence) is separate from the demonstrable well-being associations.
edges.status: No Cycle-4 evidence targeted this link.

edges.statement: Level of consciousness tracks measurable brain-state complexity (PCI) across sleep, anaesthesia and injury.
edges.status: No Cycle-4 evidence targeted this link.

edges.statement: Altered states (psychedelic, mystical) may share neural signatures such as elevated entropy.
edges.status: Unchanged (Hypothetical): slightly subcritical dynamics are reported in animal spike data, not in altered or spiritual states; non-stationary input can mimic near-criticality.

edges.statement: The geodynamo depends on core heat flow (cooling, inner-core freezing, chemical convection).
edges.status: No Cycle-4 evidence targeted this link.

edges.statement: Life and biogeochemical cycles co-evolved: microbial metabolism drives element cycles that in turn shape habitats.
edges.status: No Cycle-4 evidence targeted this link.

edges.statement: Is Earth's biota a homeostatic regulator (strong Gaia) or do biotic feedbacks often amplify change?
edges.status: Unchanged in substance; constrained-adaptation regulation depends on an assumed cost form.

edges.statement: Humans are drivers within Earth's living systems: transgressing climate or biosphere-integrity boundaries could shift the Earth system's state; ~1 million species are threatened.
edges.status: No Cycle-4 evidence targeted this link.

edges.statement: Life as Earth's soul and the core as its heart: metaphor vs literal claim.
edges.status: No Cycle-4 evidence targeted this link.

edges.statement: Consciousness's nature, the soul's existence, spirituality's causal role, geodynamo onset, Singularity/Origin remain open.
edges.status: No Cycle-4 evidence targeted this link.

edges.statement: Social relationships are associated with survival to a degree comparable with established mortality risk factors (association only).
edges.status: Unchanged (Plausible). Context: genetic-instrument evidence that loneliness and depression influence each other (a mental-side pathway, see L28); L25's body-survival association itself was not re-tested.

edges.statement: Socioeconomic deprivation is associated with higher allostatic load, a physiological marker; communal participation (religious or other) is one candidate pathway linking social conditions to health.
edges.status: No Cycle-4 evidence targeted this link.

edges.statement: Near-death reports of leaving the body: evidence about experience (consciousness studies) vs evidence about a separable soul (some traditions).
edges.status: No Cycle-4 evidence targeted this link.

edges.statement: Loneliness (felt social disconnection) and depression may causally influence each other in both directions (genetic-instrument evidence from one exploratory study).

Claims of unconscious learning and behavioural priming in Report 2's domain depend on awareness tests that are often underpowered (K09) and on paradigms that failed replication (K08).
Where the conscious/unconscious boundary is drawn (Report 5) determines what counts as subconscious; automatic processes interact with awareness rather than forming a sealed module (K07).
Track evidence describes how people, including scientists, think about souls and continuation after death (K01-K03); it informs Report 3's descriptions but not the existence question.
Kappa depends on category prevalence, so Report 3's coding-reliability statements need prevalence reported beside kappa.
Experimental awe effects on well-being and prosociality were not reproduced (K05), so they do not currently supply causal support for Report 4's spirituality-well-being links.
Mystical-type experience can be measured with acceptable psychometric fit (K04), but binary 'complete experience' classifications are noisy.
Report confounds (K13) and testability of IIT's silent-neuron predictions (K12) bear on Report 5's theory comparison (adversarial collaborations).
Sleep reactivation may be implicit while dreams are conscious fragments of reactivated memories (K10); untested here.
That self-transcendent emotion increases prosocial care (relevant to the Master Report's love question) is not supported by K05's replications and remains a hypothesis.
Contemplative accounts of pure awareness (S31, S32) connect the Consciousness topic to Report 3's accounts of the self; the connection is interpretive.
Folk intuitive materialism alongside mental-continuity judgments (K01) bears on how Report 7's Soul node is read: as a belief-structure node, not an entity.
End-of-life experiences are common among the dying and often comforting (K16). This bears on care and meaning (Report 6), not on survival of death.
Community accounts link spirituality to collective healing and resistance to oppression (K21), a Spirit x Justice bridge. It is qualitative.
Spirituality is robustly associated with lower harmful drug use (K19), but an E-value of 1.56 means modest confounding could explain it.
A presumption of consciousness for unresponsive patients (K30) extends the Master Report's care question to people who cannot show they are conscious.
Brief meditation may raise compassion via changed awareness, but the total effect was not significant (K28). This is a weak Consciousness x Love link.
How awareness is measured (objective vs subjective, post-hoc selection) changes what counts as unconscious (Report 5).
Implicit mind-body dualism persists in explicit rejecters (K15). This is relevant to Report 3's account of why soul concepts recur, but it is not evidence about souls.
Belief in free will predicts punitiveness toward everyday wrongdoing across 44 countries (K35), a reliable but small Mind x Justice link (concordance 53%).
The felt authorship of action may be a conditioned misattribution (K36). This is a coherent but untested hypothesis bearing on moral responsibility.
Calling a stimulus 'unconscious' because performance is not significantly above chance overestimates subliminal thresholds (K34; SIM-SUBC-C), which bears on Report 5's consciousness boundary.
The IIT-GNWT adversarial collaboration challenged key tenets of both theories (K42); several central failures weigh substantially against a theory, while one does not (SIM-CONS-C).
Who is judged conscious shapes decisions on life-sustaining treatment and long-term care resources (K47). This is a Consciousness x Justice bridge.

Near-death experiences are reported widely and vary by culture (K37, K46), and their memories engage autobiographical networks (K38). The evidence is small-sample and informs Report 3's account of experience, not survival.

A correlation between mystical experience and outcome can arise entirely from a common cause (SIM-SPIRIT-C), so whether the experience matters therapeutically (K39) needs manipulation, not correlation.
Dreaming under anaesthesia shows experience without environmental connection (K32). Its reported independence from awareness rests on low-powered studies.
Afterlife continuity judgments are widespread but cluster into person-level stances, and cessation is the modal response in most of 24 countries (K61; SIM-SOUL-D).
Afterlife and soul beliefs predict lower moral approval of mind upload (K55). This bears on how people judge technologies that redraw human boundaries.
The 'complete mystical experience' criterion is a 60%-on-all-subscales cut-off with good agreement but a noisy boundary (K49; SIM-SPIRIT-D).

Psychedelic trials are functionally unblinded (K51 BI 0.88-1.00), so expectancy can produce effects of the reported size (SIM-SPIRIT-D). Spirit-related therapeutic claims need expectancy-controlled designs.
Psychedelic experiences are followed by reduced death anxiety in uncontrolled pre-post studies (K52), with a prediction interval that includes zero.
Implicit bias can operate without awareness and, though small per person, can yield material group disparities in selective decisions (K56; SIM-SUBC-D). This is a Mind x Justice link.
Beliefs about agency shape punishment attitudes more than behaviour (K35, K63). Neuroscience may temper retributivism without changing legal responsibility (K57).
IIT's silent-neuron predictions are argued to be testable (K58). A second adversarial protocol (K59) can confirm large effects but rarely strong null evidence with 15 sessions (SIM-CONS-D).
Possible implicit learning and recalled death-themed experiences during deep hypothermic arrest (K60) are feasibility-level observations whose chance baseline is unknown.

edges.basis: P04 (Darwinian perspective on tumour evolution); DV0-APP-01..03
edges.statement: Tumour clonal divergence is studied with the evolutionary-biology framework (selection, drift, branching) used for species divergence.

edges.basis: P06 (phylogenies of Andic); P02 (Darwin's tree images)
edges.statement: Historical linguistics uses phylogenetic (tree) representations of divergence; the tree image itself has a contested history in Darwin's work.
Opinion fragmentation and trajectory divergence are both properties of dynamical systems; whether opinion models show sensitive dependence is untested here.
Bergson's principle of divergence and differentiation is a philosophical response to evolutionary biology, not a biological finding.
Divergence is a GAIA framework category (Proposed); this report operationalizes it per field without assuming it names one phenomenon.

edges.basis: P15 ('adapted from the Genetic Fixation Index'); DVA-NAT-07; DVA-PHI-10
edges.statement: The Cultural Fixation Index used to measure cross-country cultural divergence is adapted from the population-genetic Fst used for species divergence.
Manuscript and language divergence are analysed with the same tree-building programs as genes; contamination and borrowing play the role of horizontal gene transfer.
Tree methods could describe nested religious schisms, but such trees are recent and must not be forced onto language trees.

edges.basis: P11 (religion predicts value similarity); P15 (religion is the most divergent trait; cites P11)
edges.statement: Two independent analyses of World Values Survey data place religion at the centre of cross-country value divergence.
Cell-fate divergence pictured as a landscape can be formalised as a bifurcation of a dynamical system; whether real differentiation follows such a normal form is untested here.

edges.basis: P17 (growth factor |1 + a h|); P09 (Lyapunov exponents); DVB-APP-11; DVB-FOR-12
edges.statement: Solver instability and sensitive dependence share one mechanism: a perturbation multiplied each step by a factor of magnitude above one (|1 + a h| for forward Euler, |f'(x)| along an orbit).

Branching paired with merging gives bounded multiplicity, and stretching paired with folding gives bounded chaos; whether 'procession with reversion' or 'reversal' maps onto such pairings is a framework hypothesis only.
Divergence claims depend on the measure and the sample: slopes can mimic convergence and small families lack power, so null or opposite results need dispersion measures and power checks.
Whether something converges or diverges is a limit or population property: finite partial sums (p near 1) and selected samples (countries rich now) can show the opposite of the truth.
The Laozi's manuscript lines are a case of the copying divergence studied by stemmatics, followed by standardisation toward a received text.
Hysteresis (states that do not return when conditions reverse) is a candidate formal analogue for 'poverty traps' and stalled growth in P19; P19 does not use this model and no data here test it.

The Master Report's love theme meets the Divergence report at the return movement: love as the motive of re-ascent (Plotinus, P07) and ziran's influence on conceptions of love (P18). A framework link only.

Count-driven and selection-driven artefacts look alike: a summative originality score inherits fluency (P24), and a selected sample of rich countries shows convergence that the full sample lacks (P19); both are measurement design problems, not findings about divergence.

Divergence followed by selection or consolidation appears in idea generation (monitoring and selection, P24) and in textual transmission (standardisation of the Laozi, P18). A framework parallel only.

The giant-component fraction s = 1 - exp(-cs) (P27) is the same equation as the survival probability of a Poisson(R0) branching process, the probability that one case starts a major outbreak (IN0-APP-02: 58.3% at R0 = 1.5; IN0-FOR-02: 58.5% at c = 1.5).

Across fields, most beginnings fail: single new styles are usually lost (HUM toy), most introductions die out even above R0 = 1 (APP toy), and many riots never become revolutions (P25). A pattern across toys, not a tested law.

Insurgence and Divergence meet at thresholds: the same bifurcations that split states (DV) also let a new state rise (IN), and Bergson pairs the vital impulse with divergence. No ordering of phases is assumed.

Slow onset near threshold has the same form in the saddle-node normal form (passage time slope -0.503 in log r) and in P28's model of semantic change (-0.486 in log delta): the latency before a new linguistic form spreads is a near-critical bottleneck, as P28 argues.

Critical mass appears in both fields' models: with conformity a > 1 a preferred stance dies out below an interior threshold (P30's model), and in threshold cascades a single changed threshold stops a revolt (Granovetter, as in P25). A shared modelling pattern, not evidence that real conversions or revolts have thresholds.

A critical nucleus (P37) and a critical mass of adherents (P30's model with a > 1) play the same formal role: below it the new dissolves, above it grows, and at it the odds are near even (42% in INB-NAT-07). Whether movements have such a size threshold is not shown; P31 argues that strategy, not size alone, decides success.

Concentration matters in both: a few superspreaders produce most transmission (P32: top 17% produce 80%) and a few targeted pillars decide nonviolent campaigns (P31; agent's toy). A shared pattern, not a common mechanism.

Fluctuation-triggered onset in two engineered or natural systems: a slab stable on average ignites under temperature oscillations (P38), and a power grid can tip by noise far from any bifurcation (P41); in both the average state gives no warning, and P41 finds noise level, not slowing down, changed first.

Heavy tails from multiplication: wars grow large by compounding escalation factors (P39) and outbreaks by heterogeneous offspring (P32); in both most beginnings stay small and a few become very large. The mechanisms differ (multiplicative growth in time vs branching).

Onset at a critical connection probability: a percolating path appears abruptly near q = 0.59 (P44/P45), and simple contagion on random networks takes off just above P40's threshold p1* = 1/3; in both a small change in local transmission switches the whole system from contained to spanning.

Reinforcement must be strong to change the outcome qualitatively: clustered networks gain an advantage only under near-deterministic reinforcement (P40), and in P30's model a conversion outlasts its occasion only with super-linear conformity (a > 1). Different models; the parallel is the agent's.

Cooperative binding and the fusion loop share positive feedback: each bond (NAT) or each act of deviance answered by condemnation (SOC) makes the next more likely, giving steep, threshold-like responses. Analogy between toys, not a shared mechanism.

Direct reciprocity needs a high chance w of another round (P47) and loyalty keeps members in an institution long enough for voice to work (P51): in both, cooperation pays only when the relationship is expected to continue.

Allegiance and Insurgence meet where loyal groups resist or join an uprising: fusion predicts readiness to fight for the group (P48) and minority languages persist under majority pressure (P50). No ordering of phases is assumed.

In both fields a verdict depends on the size of the sample relative to the effect: the 1/3 rule misses by 6% at N s = 0.5 but holds at weak selection (FOR), and P49's null for allegiance would still be missed 4 times in 10 with 100 studies (APP).

Printed summary statistics allow outside re-checks: P49's p value and power follow from its beta and SE, while one of P52's six key SEM signs (Study 3 fusion -> violence) cannot be reproduced from its printed correlations.

Checking printed numbers against data or confidence intervals changes conclusions: P52's unreproducible path is a transposed table (SOC), and P56's null for developer involvement, unlike P49's, has the power to exclude effects of 0.2 (APP).

Loyalty as P59 describes it can be forfeited when its object proves unworthy, whereas identity fusion (P52) goes with readiness for violent action; the contrast suggests that forfeitability may mark the difference between loyalty and fusion (agent's hypothesis, untested).

A summary can be well determined while its parts are not: the maximal Hill slope of one binding curve is precise while the Adair constants are not (NAT), as a meta-analytic mean can be precise while moderators are not (APP).

Royce's criterion (a cause is good insofar as it furthers others' loyalty; 'predatory' loyalty is evil) offers a test for P61's 'bright side' of fusion: fusion that raises intergroup prosocial intention would count as loyalty to loyalty, fusion with violent intent (P52) as predatory; P61's own evidence for the bright side is weaker than printed (Tukey contrast not supported). Agent's hypothesis, untested.

Re-computing printed statistics from printed summaries is cheap and finds real issues: an unnamed post hoc test that Tukey does not support (P61) and an allegiance-balanced trial whose null cannot exclude clinically relevant differences (P54).

Lumping hides structure: a binding curve that looks like one weakly cooperative state can be two non-cooperative populations (P62), as 'Chinese' in heritage-language research can hide a non-officialised variety (P60). Agent's analogy.

Frequency dependence makes switching allegiance hard: in P58's Moran model a new convention's required basin grows toward 1 with selection strength, and in the three-language toy the smaller language loses even with higher status.

P59's forfeiture and P63's atonement are two answers to betrayal; in repeated games retaliation alone (TFT) never ends the feud, while forgiveness or contrition restores cooperation at a lasting small cost. Agent's analogy, not a reading of either source.

Researcher allegiance reaches meta-analysis: P66, by fusion-theory originators, finds fusion beats identification only in published studies, and the unpublished null is informative (power 0.95), so the published advantage may partly reflect publication or allegiance effects. Plausible; P66 itself discusses publication bias but not author allegiance.

Two current readings of haemoglobin disagree: P64 fits the two-state MWC model without tertiary states, while P62 finds the T state heterogeneous. With P64's constants the MWC curve lands near measured P50 and slope, so the simple model is adequate at the level of whole curves even if P62's heterogeneity is real.
Ruth adopts Naomi's people and God by choice, the reverse of the heritage loyalty P65 studies; both treat allegiance as chosen identity rather than given by birth. Agent's analogy.

Stable coexistence of loyalties needs weak frequency dependence: in the three-language toy only a < 1 keeps all varieties, as in P58's Moran model a weak-selection basin stays near 1/3 while strong selection shifts it. Agent's analogy.

DeGroot averaging with a stochastic matrix converges to a consensus weighted by the chain's equilibrium vector (CV0-FOR-02), the same weighted-average form as P69's centralized estimate a_n(omega); a central agent is one with a large equilibrium weight.

In both toys convergence needs the units to be coupled to the same signal: oscillators lock only while the deviating share stays below a bound, and inquirers merge only if their priors give weight to the truth and the evidence can separate hypotheses. Analogy, not a shared mechanism.

Convergence is the reverse direction of Divergence on the same objects: the two-cluster state that persists below P68's bound splits into incoherence above it, and a periodic chain never converges. No ordering of phases is assumed.

P74's null model of molecular convergence is a two-state Markov chain per locus with equilibrium S = P_gain/(P_gain + P_loss) (P74 Eq. 1), the same object as P73's regular chains; the decay of chance overlap is governed by the second eigenvalue 1 - P_gain - P_loss.

A fully stubborn agent in DeGroot averaging fixes the consensus at its own opinion, the limit omega = 1 of P69's centralized estimate; P69 and CVA-SOC-04 show that partial centralization changes accuracy only modestly with the weight.

Peirce contrasts convergence of inquiry with settling opinion by authority, where 'the idea of loyalty replaced that of truth-seeking' (P75): one textual point of contact between the Convergence and Allegiance phases. No ordering of phases is assumed.

The mixing time defined in P78 measures how long P74's per-locus null chain needs to forget its start: with P_loss 0.005 it is 186 steps (My) for eps = 1/4 and 698 for eps = 0.01, so the chance-overlap null is near equilibrium only for the older species pairs in P74's 0-682 My range.

In both toys a component that never updates blocks convergence: two stubborn DeGroot agents prevent consensus, and never-improving methods keep Peirce's investigators apart. Analogy between agent-built models, not a shared mechanism.

Limit formulas hold only near their limit: P76's small-mu synchronisation formula is accurate at mu 0.03 and gives r > 1 at mu 0.57, and P79's asymptotic quadrature error predicts the needed N to 1% but has the wrong sign for f3 at N = 8.

edges.basis: CVC-PHI-07; CVC-HUM-07; CVC-HUM-06; CVC-PHI-06; P81; P82
edges.statement: Contact produces convergence that can mimic common origin: dialects level toward the majority through contact (P82), and in the agent's toy widespread contact between traditions yields similarity without a distance gradient, like a common core; in both cases the history of contact, not the similarity itself, decides between the explanations.

Finite systems approach their limit with a sharpening transition: the riffle shuffle's distance falls from above 0.9 to 0.1 within 3-4 shuffles at every deck size (cutoff), and the Kuramoto order parameter's incoherent floor falls as N^-1/2 while the critical point decays more slowly; both are agent computations on P78's and P76's models.

edges.basis: CVD-PHI-12; CVD-PHI-14; CVD-APP-10; P83; P84; P79
edges.statement: Whether things 'agree' depends on the instrument and its tolerance: two quadrature rules need the same 3 nodes at 0.1% but 5 vs 15 at 1e-6, and an instrument that measures three of six dimensions finds no tradition difference while the unmeasured dimensions differ; P83's null across traditions had only 53% power at f 0.15. Absence of detected difference is not evidence of sameness.

The direction of social convergence depends on context more than on any single bias: in the copying toy majority-amplifying copying overrides a weak prestige bias, and in P69's estimation model the advantage of centralization reverses sign with the bias and dispersion of the initial estimates.

An adaptive walk is discrete hill climbing: each step moves to a fitter neighbour, the discrete counterpart of following the gradient; on a smooth (additive) landscape there is one peak and every walk reaches it (AS0-NAT-02 V1), as gradient flow reaches the unique optimum of a contracting system (AS0-FOR-02), while ruggedness adds local peaks that trap walks.

Both audited ascent studies have headline numbers that need care: P87's Table 5 reduction does not follow from its deviances (77.8% vs 78.8%), and P88's 2.069 is a risk ratio although Fig. 2 calls it odds (the odds ratio is 9.6); the underlying findings stand.

In both toys ascent stops at a local level unless something moves it on: a walk stops at any peak with no fitter neighbour, and the lover stays on a rung unless an uncovered case meets the disposition to resolve it. Analogy, not a shared mechanism.

Ascent toward an optimum is convergence seen from the objective: contracting gradient flow converges to its optimum (AS0-FOR-02), and adaptive walks converge on peaks, high or low (AS0-NAT-02). No ordering of phases is assumed.

Getting stuck below the top: adaptive walks stop at local peaks of rugged landscapes (the global peak is reached in under 1% of walks at K 5), and majority-amplifying copying fixes a community on the majority variant; in both toys moving to a higher or minority state needs something beyond local improvement or copying. Analogy, not a shared mechanism.

Ascent has a safe speed: gradient steps converge only below a step-size limit (dt < 1 for P86's natural gradient, eta < 0.002 for plain steps), and faster physical ascent raises AMS risk at the first stage (P88; P91 at 3650 m), although P91 finds the order reversed at the second stage. Analogy, not a shared mechanism.

Where an ascent ends depends on where it starts: walks reach high peaks through their large basins, and plain gradient steps converge or diverge depending on the start even below the local step limit. Analogy, not a shared mechanism.

Upward change meets inherited structure: rising intonation is evaluated differently by listener age (P92), a minority variant rises in the toy only without majority amplification, and class or educational ascent grows only as inheritance weakens (P87, P93). Analogy, not a shared mechanism.

Correlation makes ascent reliable: in correlated (RMF) landscapes the global peak is almost always reachable by uphill paths, whereas in uncorrelated (HoC) ones it usually is not (P94; agent's counts); in optimisation, a metric matched to the problem (natural gradient) makes descent converge from every start, while plain steps fail from some. Analogy, not a shared mechanism.

Rate and structure both bound an ascent: faster physical ascent raises AMS risk (P95 RR 1.60) on top of the altitude reached, and class ascent is bounded by structural change (minimum mobility) on top of inheritance. Analogy, not a shared mechanism.

Ascent depends on the shape of the space: absolute upward mobility follows structural upgrading while relative mobility follows inheritance (P96; rank toy), and uphill paths to the global peak exist when fitness is correlated across neighbouring genotypes (P94; path counts). Analogy, not a shared mechanism.

Thresholds decide rises: in the copying toy a minority variant rises only above a start-share threshold (about 18-19% at c 1.5, b 1.0), and in the ladder toy a lover rises only when disposition outweighs regress. Both are the agent's toys. Analogy, not a shared mechanism.

Both baseline checks rest on growth rates of iterated linear maps or expansions: P97's life-cycle fitness is the log dominant eigenvalue of a projection matrix (confirmed by iteration to 1e-8), and P98's sanity measures how fast the digits of an expansion pin a number down; both separate a short-run quantity from a long-run one.

All three audited self-transcendence studies have printed numbers that do not follow from their own inputs (P99's Power mean and participant flow; P100's chance agreement and Bartlett df; P101's vastness BF01 and wording), while their main test statistics reproduce.

Experiences described as transcending the self are studied through reports: P101's sublime ratings and P102's mystics' accounts; the PHI toy shows report agreement can arise from a shared background as well as from a common core. Analogy, not a shared mechanism.

Transcendence as a transition to a new level of individuality differs from ascent within one landscape: P97's tradeoff breaking moves the feasible set rather than climbing within it (TR0-NAT-02, both F and f2 rise). No ordering of phases is assumed; the owner's level mapping is not tested.

structure_edges_note: Organisational relations (which report a topic deepens; which reports feed the Master Report). Not evidential claims, so no E/P/PS/H label.
